humidity-limit-symbol.context: An umbrella canopy over a single water drop. It is the handling mark telling people to keep a package dry, printed on boxes and cartons for shipping and storage.

protect-from-light.context: A box under a roof with a sun and rays above it. It marks goods that must be kept out of sunlight, such as light sensitive medicine, film and food.

handle-with-care.context: A box held in two cupped hands. Used on parcels and crates as the fragile or handle carefully mark, and for any item that needs gentle treatment.

open-here.context: A box with a pull strip across its front and an arrow above pointing along the tear line. It shows where to tear open a carton or parcel.

tear-notch.context: A pouch with a small V cut in its edge and a dashed tear line running from it. It shows where to tear a sachet or packet open.

keep-refrigerated.context: A box with a snowflake next to a thermometer. It tells people to store a product cold, used on food, medicine and chilled deliveries.

tamper-evident-seal.context: A jar lid above a neck ring whose band is torn in a zigzag. It stands for tamper evident seals that show if a container has been opened.
keywords: do not use if seal broken

child-resistant-cap.context: A bottle cap with a downward push arrow and a curved turn arrow. It shows the push down and turn action needed to open a childproof lid.

small-parts-warning.context: A circle crossed by a slash around a solid round head. It is the toy warning that a product is not suitable for very young children because of choking risk.

plastic-bag-suffocation-warning.context: A plastic bag with a small head inside, crossed out. It warns that bags can cause suffocation and must be kept away from babies and small children.

keep-out-of-reach-of-children.context: A bottle on a high shelf with a small child reaching up from below. It is the packaging warning to store medicine and chemicals where children cannot get them.
keywords: keep out of reach of children

stovetop-safe.context: A pan resting on a burner line with flame strokes beneath it. Used on cookware labels to show that a pot or pan can go on a gas or hob cooking surface.

recyclable-carton.context: A drink carton inside a loop of three chasing arrows. It marks a carton as recyclable and is printed on juice, milk and soup packs.

recycled-content.context: A solid circle holding a white loop of three chasing arrows. It is the mark for packaging made from recycled material.

refillable-symbol.context: A bottle with a circular arrow on its body. It tells people the container can be refilled and used again, common on cleaning and personal care packs.

sharps-disposal.context: A box with a slotted lid and a syringe pushed needle first into the slot. It marks a container for used needles and other medical sharps.

oil-recycling.context: A single oil drop inside a loop of three chasing arrows. It marks collection for used cooking oil or motor oil so it can be recycled.

litter-bin-symbol.context: A figure dropping a piece of litter into a bin beside it. It is the keep it tidy sign asking people to use a bin instead of dropping rubbish.

austral-sign.context: A capital A crossed by two horizontal bars. It is the austral, the former currency sign of Argentina, used in currency lists and old price tables.

degrees-minutes-seconds.context: A degree ring, a prime and a double prime above an angle wedge. It stands for angles and map coordinates written in degrees, minutes and seconds.

power-set-symbol.context: The script lowercase p with a looped tail, called the Weierstrass p. In set theory it writes the power set, the collection of all subsets of a set.

laplace-transform.context: A flowing script capital L with a looped top and a curled foot. It stands for the Laplace transform used to solve differential equations and analyse systems.

nabla.context: An upside down triangle with a small f beside it. The nabla or del operator writes gradient, divergence and curl in vector calculus and physics.

cycloid.context: A circle resting on a flat line beneath the arch traced by a point on its rim as it rolls. Used to show the cycloid curve in geometry and physics lessons.

lissajous-curve.context: A smooth closed curve that crosses itself in a knotted pattern, traced by two sine waves at different frequencies. Seen on oscilloscopes and in harmonic motion demos.

rose-curve.context: A four petal flower shape drawn by a single curve with all petals meeting at the centre. Used for rose or rhodonea curves in polar coordinate lessons.

catenary.context: A chain hanging in a smooth U between the tops of two posts. The catenary is the curve of a hanging cable, seen in power lines, bridges and arches.

hilbert-curve.context: A single line folding through a square in right angle turns, the Hilbert curve. It stands for space filling curves, fractals and recursive patterns.

voronoi-diagram.context: A square divided into irregular polygon cells, each holding one seed dot. A Voronoi diagram groups space by nearest point, used in maps, graphics and data science.

optical-radiation-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a small sun and bold rays at its centre. It warns of hazardous light such as lasers, UV and bright optical sources.

lightning-strike-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a lightning bolt striking down toward a small standing figure. It warns of lightning risk in open or outdoor work areas.

fragile-roof-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a figure falling through a broken gap in a roof sheet. It warns that a roof or skylight will not take a person's weight.

door-finger-trap-hazard.context: A warning triangle with fingers reaching into the hinge gap beside a door edge. It warns of a crush or pinch point where fingers can be trapped.

robot-arm-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a jointed robot arm reaching out from its base. It warns of moving industrial machinery that can swing into people.

high-pressure-jet-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a nozzle sending a straight jet of liquid that ends in drops. It warns of high pressure spray that can injure skin.

radio-frequency-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a mast antenna sending curved waves to both sides. It warns of radio frequency radiation near transmitters and masts.

wear-face-mask-sign.context: A solid round sign with a head wearing a face mask over its nose and mouth. It is the mandatory sign requiring a mask in clinics, labs and shared spaces.

use-hand-sanitizer-sign.context: A solid round sign with a pump bottle dispensing a drop onto a hand. It is the mandatory sign asking people to sanitise their hands.

shake-well.context: An upright bottle with curved motion lines on both sides. It is the instruction to shake a bottle before use, found on medicine, paint and drinks.

peel-here.context: A tray with a film lid whose corner is peeling back and an arrow pointing to the flap. It shows where to start peeling the film from a ready meal or pot.

resealable-pack.context: A pouch with a zip seal track across its top and an arrow pointing up to it. It marks a bag that can be closed again after opening.

pierce-film-lid.context: A shallow tray covered with film and a fork piercing down into it. It is the heating instruction to prick the lid before putting a meal in the microwave.

manufacturer-symbol.context: A solid factory outline with a sawtooth roof and a chimney. It is the label symbol that precedes the maker's name and address on medical devices.

lot-number-symbol.context: The letters L, O and T standing together. It marks the batch or lot code printed on medicines, devices and food so a product can be traced.

single-use-symbol.context: A numeral 2 inside a circle crossed by a slash. It is the label symbol meaning do not reuse a device, found on syringes, swabs and other disposables.

pattern-blocks.context: A hexagon divided into a trapezoid, a rhombus and two triangles. It stands for pattern block tiles used to teach shapes, fractions and symmetry in classrooms.

fraction-strips.context: Three stacked bars of equal length, one whole, one split in halves and one in thirds. Used to compare fractions in primary maths.

multiplication-array.context: A grid of dots in three rows of four. Arrays like this show how rows times columns gives a product when learning times tables.

bar-model.context: A long bar split into three parts with a bracket above marking the total. Bar models help children solve part and whole word problems.
